about: H1 (prompts/phase-01-topology.md step 5): hand-written id pairs for makeEdgeId. The oracle orders undirected endpoints with localeCompare (src/core/model/ids.ts, stable sort, so a 0 keeps argument order); graph-core orders them by UTF-8 bytes. `diverges` says whether the two orderings pick a different first endpoint for at least one argument order. harness/oracle-diff.mjs checks every declaration against what it observes, so a wrong line here fails the differential. Non-ASCII is written as escapes so no editor can renormalise it.

pairs.why: case: ICU puts lowercase first at the tertiary level; bytes put 'A' (0x41) before 'a' (0x61)
the Z/a boundary: ICU sorts alphabetically across case; bytes put every uppercase letter first
a realistic prefixed id pair differing only in case
the tag prefix, differing only in case
a record id differing only in case after two equal coordinates
uppercase before lowercase in bytes, alphabetical in ICU
punctuation: ICU ranks '_' before '-'; bytes put '-' (0x2D) before '_' (0x5F)
an accented letter sorts with its base letter in ICU and after all ASCII in bytes
as above, uppercase accented
ICU ranks the symbol before letters; bytes put the 4-byte sequence last
ICU ranks the symbol before the ideograph; bytes put the astral code point last
UTF-16 code-unit order and UTF-8 byte order disagree here too (surrogates sort below U+FF21): the contract is UTF-8 bytes, not JavaScript's `<`
canonically equivalent (NFC vs NFD): localeCompare returns 0, so the oracle keeps argument order and A-B, B-A do not collapse; bytes order them one way
control: both put '_x' first
control: both put 'e' first
control: localeCompare without the numeric option compares digit by digit, as bytes do
